items.title: Genie ZeroOps is available in Beta
items.text: Genie ZeroOps is now available in Beta. It monitors jobs, pipelines, and tables in the background, detects failures and data quality issues, investigates the root cause, and proposes a fix. See Get started with Genie ZeroOps.

items.title: Azure Databricks Genie plugin for Microsoft Copilot Cowork (Public Preview)
items.text: The Azure Databricks Genie plugin connects Microsoft Copilot Cowork to Genie One, so users can ask questions about their Azure Databricks data without creating an OAuth app or editing a plugin manifest. Existing installations of the Beta manifest-based Genie plugin aren't migrated automatically. To use the new plugin, add it in Copilot Cowork. See Azure Databricks Genie plugin for Microsoft Copilot Cowork.

items.title: Pages are generally available
items.text: Pages, governed definitions of business concepts organized by domain on the Discover page, are generally available. Curators can certify and deprecate Pages, and the new MANAGE PAGES permission controls who can publish and manage Pages in a domain. You can also manage Pages with the REST API. See Pages.

items.title: The Genie One desktop app for Windows is in Beta
items.text: The Genie One desktop app is now available for Windows in Beta, in addition to macOS. The native app opens Genie One on your desktop instead of in a browser tab, so business users can chat with data in natural language, work with their threads and documents, and use Genie Agents without a browser. See Windows.

items.title: Write custom service policies in Python (Beta)
items.text: You can now write a custom service policy as a Python function in Unity Catalog. Use it for rules that SQL can't express, such as regular expressions, Python packages, or calls to an external guardrail through a service credential. It's available in select regions. See Write a custom Python service policy.

items.title: Text and binary inputs for protobuf requests to custom model serving endpoints (Public Preview)
items.text: Protobuf requests to custom model serving endpoints can now carry text and binary data, such as titles, images, audio, and documents, as KServe v2 BYTES tensors alongside numeric tensors in the same request. Text and binary model outputs are returned as BYTES tensors. This feature is in Public Preview and is only available on endpoints deployed after November 10, 2026. See Protobuf tensor input.

items.title: External access to Unity Catalog managed Delta tables will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
items.text: Starting on or after December 10, 2026, external access to Unity Catalog managed Delta tables will be available by default for eligible workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Supported external Delta clients can create, read, and write Unity Catalog managed Delta tables. Creating and writing managed Delta tables requires catalog commits. Metastore external data access settings and Unity Catalog privileges continue to control access. See Access Databricks tables from Delta clients.

items.title: The next chapter for CI/CD in Fabric Warehouse (Preview)
items.text: Sections: What we've delivered; Establishing a consistent deployment foundation with DacFx; Pre, and post-deployment scripts; Warehouse Item Definition APIs; Bringing Familiar Warehouse Development Experiences to Client Tools; What's next for CI/CD in Fabric Warehouse; Get started with CI/CD in Fabric Warehouse. Building and operating a data warehouse is increasingly a software engineering discipline. Teams want to develop warehouse changes in isolation, version them in Git, review them through pull requests, promote them safely across environments, and automate the entire process using their existing CI/CD systems. Over the past several releases, we've been evolving CI/CD in Fabric Warehouse around that lifecycle: DacFx established a common schema deployment foundation. Pre, and post-deployment scripts expanded deployments beyond schema changes. Warehouse Item Definition APIs opened the same lifecycle to automation. items.title: Use OneLake as native storage for Azure Databricks (Preview)
items.text: Sections: Why this matters; What's new in this release; One shared data foundation, with flexibility above it; Use OneLake as the storage foundation; Continue using Unity Catalog-managed objects; Keep platform responsibilities clear; How it works; Security; How to read the data in Fabric; Get started. Organizations increasingly use Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databricks together so teams can choose the tools that best fit their data engineering, analytics, and AI workloads while working from a common data foundation. OneLake external-location support for Azure Databricks Unity Catalog is now generally available in Microsoft Fabric, with OneLake Security enabled by default for Azure Databricks Storage items. On the Azure Databricks side, the feature is in preview. With this integration, supported Unity Catalog-managed data can be stored directly in OneLake.
